requirements.evidence: Everything in the contract is there: the migrations with cascades, the unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:15-30); Queue with fillable and casts (Queue.php:11-27); Entity::queues(); both enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket rejects a negative priority before the transaction, locks the queue row and re-reads is_active ('Queue::query()->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail', IssueTicket.php:48-52), and retries 3 times on UniqueConstraintViolationException. nextCode walks the codes by id in descending order and skips malformed ones (Ticket.php:85-96). The write-once updating guard is at Ticket.php:48-69. call() authorizes through a policy, locks the row and throws LogicException when the ticket is not waiting. The factory has a lazy code closure and forQueue(). One gap: nextCode derives from the tickets that remain, so deleting the newest ticket lets its number be reused, which contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'. The docs even record this (business-rules.md: 'Deleting the most recently issued ticket makes its number the next one again').

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through app/Actions/IssueTicket. Authorization goes through app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php ('Gate::forUser($user)->authorize('call', $this)'). Fillable is set deliberately with the #[Fillable] attribute. Migrations have reversible down() and generated-style timestamps. PHPDoc is on the public methods. CHANGELOG, business-rules.md, database-schema.md and architecture.md are all updated. Small deviations: an extra root-level tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php sits beside the tests/Feature/Queue/ files, and the docs describe a deletion rule that differs from the spec instead of following it.

security.evidence: call() authorizes through a policy before any write, and the outsider and other-entity tests confirm the ticket is unchanged. The write-once guard blocks changes to the other fields. The queue state is read under a row lock instead of trusting the caller's model. There is no HTTP or Livewire surface. The fillable lists are explicit (Ticket.php:16, Queue.php:11).

tests.evidence: The tests cover the full rule set. Queue/TicketCodeTest covers A001..A003, A999 -> A1000 -> A1001, deletion in the middle -> A004, malformed codes, insertion order and per-queue sequences. Queue/IssueTicketTest covers defaults, priority and channel, negative priority and inactive queues persisting nothing, a stale deactivated queue, collision retry and giving up after 3 attempts. Queue/TicketWriteOnceTest has a dataset over every immutable field. Queue/TicketCallTest covers all roles, outsiders, other-entity members, single call and a stale instance. Schema and cascade tests are in TicketSchemaTest and QueueModelTest. No test covers deleting the newest ticket, which is the case the implementation gets wrong.

simplicity.evidence: The production code is lean: the retry loop is small, nextCode is a single lazyByIdDesc/first query, and the policy is one line. tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php (178 lines) largely repeats tests in tests/Feature/Queue/*, for example 'allocates sequential codes', 'rejects a negative priority', the malformed-code cases and the forQueue A001/A002 case.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the constants are named (MAX_ATTEMPTS, CALL_FIELDS, CODE_PATTERN). The comments explain why ('the caller's instance may be stale', 'Query-builder bulk updates bypass model events'). The updating closure (Ticket.php:50-68) packs two concerns, field immutability and the state transition, into one long closure. The collision test says 'the next free code' but asserts A001, because the colliding row is rolled back together with the failed attempt.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Replacing the TODO in docs/architecture.md is related. The duplicate root-level test file is redundant rather than out of scope. The extra QueueFactory::inactive() state is small and used by the tests.

issues.explanation: The next code is computed from the tickets that remain, so deleting the newest ticket (e.g. A003 after A001..A003) makes A003 the next code again; the task says deleting a ticket does not reuse its number, and the docs record this deviation instead of fixing it.

This second test file largely duplicates cases already in tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php, TicketCodeTest.php, TicketCallTest.php and TicketWriteOnceTest.php, so the suite is larger without covering more.
No test covers deleting the most recently issued ticket, which is where the no-reuse rule breaks.
The test name says the ticket is issued with 'the next free code', but it asserts A001 because the colliding insert rolls back with the failed attempt; the name misdescribes what the test checks.
The updating closure mixes the immutability check with state-transition validation; two small private methods would read more clearly.

review.summary: The change adds the queue and ticket schema, models, enums, factories, a policy-authorized single call, a write-once guard and the IssueTicket action with an in-transaction queue lock and collision retry, plus thorough tests and doc updates. It meets almost every contract item and follows the conventions, but deleting the newest ticket lets its number be reused, which contradicts the no-reuse rule (the docs acknowledge this), and one test file is a duplicate. Approve after fixing the code-reuse edge case.
